text:
india: quick UX check: in invite drawer with SSO enforced we disable 'Assign roles' button. design wants clearer affordance so people know why they can't assign. options: inline badge, help link, deep-link to audit.
noah: deep-link to audit history seems most actionable. people want context.
emma: agree but from a11y POV disabled button should keep `aria-disabled` and we should add an accessible link below it instead of making the disabled control interactive.
devon: implementation note: adding `/audit?event=invite.role&role=Admin` is trivial. badge non-interactive is easiest; tooltip will be dynamic based on org.sso_mode.
a11y-bot: scan: invite-drawer frame flagged: disabled control removed from tab order; recommend `aria-disabled="true"` and a sibling link with `aria-label="Open audit history filtered to role Admin"`. Also don't rely on title attribute for tooltips.
india: proposed decision: 1) leave CTA visually disabled + `aria-disabled`. 2) add secondary link text 'View audit history for this role' under CTA that deep-links with filters. 3) show inline non-interactive badge 'SSO managed' with tooltip using `aria-describedby`. 4) avoid modal this sprint.
emma: copy suggestions: tooltip: "Role assignments are managed by your identity provider. Contact your admin." audit link: "View audit history for this role" badge tooltip: "Managed by SSO".
noah: timeline: devs can implement next sprint if product confirms copy by Thu EOD.
devon: ok assigned; will add tests to assert query params and aria-label.
a11y-bot: checklist: disabled control `aria-disabled`, audit link keyboard focusable, accessible tooltip pattern, aria-label includes role and event filters.
india: thanks all — i'll update figma and post final copy here.
